caption:
NVIDIA's RTX Spark laptops go on sale today, starting at $2,599.99.
The chip pairs Arm CPU cores with a Blackwell GPU and up to 128GB of memory.
NVIDIA says it can run 120B-parameter AI models right on the laptop.

Would you pay $2,599 for a laptop that runs big AI models offline?

Follow @neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: Windows Central · Photo: Kevin Lee / The Shortcut

slides.headline: Windows laptops can now run *giant AI models offline*. NVIDIA's RTX Spark goes on sale today

slides.heading: A chip *built for AI*
paras: RTX Spark pairs up to 20 Arm-based Grace CPU cores with a Blackwell RTX GPU. NVIDIA built it with MediaTek.
Top models carry up to 128GB of unified memory. NVIDIA rates the chip at up to 1 petaflop of AI performance.

slides.heading: Big models, *no cloud*
paras: NVIDIA says the chip can run 120-billion-parameter AI models on the laptop itself, with tools like Ollama, LM Studio and llama.cpp.
In The Shortcut's hands-on, Alan Wake 2 ran with ray tracing at well over 60 fps, and Premiere Pro is reported to run about 2x faster.

slides.heading: The *price tag*
paras: Prices start at $2,599.99 for Microsoft's Surface Laptop Ultra and the ASUS ProArt P14. Dell's XPS 16 Creator Edition starts at $3,799.99.
Microsoft, ASUS, Dell, HP, Lenovo and MSI all have RTX Spark laptops. Compact desktops follow in November.

slides.heading: The *big question*
paras: RTX Spark runs Windows on Arm, which has struggled with some games' anti-cheat software in the past. Some games run through emulation.
Independent benchmarks are only starting to arrive, so battery life and game support still need real-world testing.

paras.t: Launch day is here. The verdict is not.

slides.hook: RTX Spark could change what a laptop can do with AI. Follow to see how it holds up in real tests.
